#


Quicknode Now Supports Arc Mainnet


Arc mainnet is live and Quicknode Arc RPC access is available from day one. Create an Arc endpoint and start building on the stablecoin-native L1.


[Quicknode](https://www.quicknode.com/blog/author/quicknode)


September 16, 2026 — 2 min read


Arc mainnet is live, and Quicknode Arc RPC access is available from day one. Developers can[create an Arc RPC endpoint](https://www.quicknode.com/chains/arc) right now and start building on the open, EVM-compatible Layer-1 designed for financial markets, real-time money movement, and agentic economic activity.


## What is Arc?


Arc launches as the Economic OS for the internet: an open, EVM-compatible Layer-1 blockchain for the world's financial markets, real-time money movement, and agentic economic activity. From day one, Arc brings together USDC, local fiat stablecoins, tokenized assets, programmable Bitcoin, and leading onchain applications in one connected ecosystem. Learn more at[arc.io](https://www.arc.io/) .


Three things stand out at launch:


-


Stablecoins as gas, starting with USDC, so fees are predictable and dollar-based


-


Deterministic sub-second finality, which matters for payments, trading, and FX


-


Live markets from day one: lending, borrowing, trading, onchain FX, payments, and tokenized assets


Behind it all sits a geo-diverse, known institutional validator set.


## Arc Mainnet RPC access on Quicknode


Quicknode supports Arc with full RPC access from launch. Because Arc is EVM-compatible, existing Ethereum tooling, libraries, and workflows carry over. If you have built on any EVM chain, you already know how to build on Arc.


An[Arc RPC endpoint](https://www.quicknode.com/chains/arc) on Quicknode comes with the same global infrastructure, reliability, and developer experience available across every chain Quicknode supports, so teams can partner with Circle to build on Arc without standing up their own nodes.


Arc Mainnet support on Quicknode covers more than RPC:


Capability


What you get on Arc


Docs


[Core RPC API](https://www.quicknode.com/core-api)


JSON-RPC over HTTPS and WSS, with every EVM method supported


[Arc API overview](https://www.quicknode.com/docs/arc/api-overview)


Archive, debug, and trace


Full archive nodes, including debug_traceTransaction and debug_traceBlockByNumber


[debug_traceTransaction](https://www.quicknode.com/docs/arc/debug_traceTransaction)


## How to get your Arc RPC URL


1.


Log in to the[Quicknode dashboard](https://dashboard.quicknode.com/) or[create a free account](https://www.quicknode.com/signup)


2.


Create a new endpoint and select Arc Mainnet


3.


Copy your Arc RPC URL and point your application at it


That's it. Full setup instructions, supported methods, and network details are in the[Arc documentation](https://www.quicknode.com/docs/arc) , and the[Arc chain page](https://www.quicknode.com/chains/arc) has current network information.
